questions.question: On a place-value chart the columns from left to right are billions, hundred millions, ten millions, millions, hundred thousands, ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, ones — ten columns in all. A card with the digit 7 is placed in the billions column, and a 0 card is placed in every one of the other nine columns. What number is on the chart?
questions.explain: The billions column is the tenth column from the ones, so the number needs the 7 plus nine zeros: 7 000 000 000. A common trap is saying seven million — millions need only six zeros, and every placeholder zero has to be counted, not guessed.

questions.question: A place-value chart for decimals has four columns: ones, tenths, hundredths, thousandths. A 4 card goes in the ones column, a 0 card in the tenths column, a 0 card in the hundredths column, and a 6 card in the thousandths column. What number is on the chart?
questions.explain: Every column must keep its own digit, so the tenths and hundredths zeros stay: 4.006. The usual trap is erasing those zeros and writing 4.6, which would put the 6 in the tenths column instead of the thousandths column.

questions.question: The digits of the number 4 072 000 000 are placed one per column on a place-value chart, starting at the far left. Reading left to right the digits are 4, 0, 7, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 — ten digits in ten columns. Which place is the digit 7 sitting in?
questions.explain: Ten digits means the far-left column is billions, so the columns run billions, hundred millions, ten millions — the 7 is the third digit, so it is in the ten millions place. The trap is skipping over the 0 in the hundred millions column, which slides every digit one place too high.

questions.question: On a place-value chart, a 5 card is placed in the billions column, a 2 card is placed in the hundred millions column, and a 0 card is placed in every other column all the way down to the ones. How is this number read aloud?
questions.explain: Read each group of three digits and then name its group: 5 200 000 000 is five billion, two hundred million. The trap is dropping down a whole group and saying million where the chart says billion, or thousand where it says million.

questions.question: A news app says a national transit fund is worth three billion, forty million, five hundred thousand dollars. Which is that amount in standard form?
questions.explain: Fill the groups from the left: 3 billions, 040 millions, 500 thousands, 000 ones, giving $3 040 500 000. The trap is forgetting the placeholder zeros inside forty million (040, not 400) — a missing or extra zero changes the amount by ten times.

questions.question: At a school track meet in Kamloops the electronic timer shows Jamal's 100 m time as 12.045 seconds. How is this time read aloud?
options: twelve and four hundred fifty thousandths
questions.explain: Read the digits after the point as one number, then name the last place: 045 ends in the thousandths column, so it is twelve and forty-five thousandths. The trap is ignoring the 0 right after the point, which turns 12.045 into the much larger 12.45.

questions.question: A government website lists last year's spending on BC ferries and highways as $6 328 145 900. What is the value of the digit 3 in that amount?
questions.explain: The amount has ten digits, so the places run billions, hundred millions, ten millions...; the 3 is the second digit, so it is worth $300 000 000. The trap is grabbing the whole group name and saying three billion — only the first digit is in the billions place.

questions.question: Aria's aunt has to write the amount $2 003 070 in words on a cheque for a community centre. Which word form is correct?
questions.explain: Split into groups — 2 | 003 | 070 — and name each: two million, three thousand, seventy. The trap is dropping a placeholder zero and reading 003 as thirty or 070 as hundred, which changes the size of the cheque.

questions.question: A news post about a BC wildfire recovery fund shows the amount $1 200 000 000. Maya reads it as one billion two hundred million dollars. Owen reads it as one million two hundred thousand dollars. Who is right, and why?
options: Maya, because the amount has ten digits, so the 1 sits in the billions place.
Owen, because 1 200 000 000 has the same digits as 1 200 000, so it is read the same way.
Owen, because any number this long is read in millions once it passes nine digits.
Owen, because the 1 sits in the millions place.
questions.explain: Count the digits or the groups of three: ten digits means the leading digit is in the billions place, so the fund is one billion two hundred million dollars. The trap is judging by the shape of the digits instead of counting the zeros — a billion has three more zeros than a million, so the two amounts are 1000 times apart.

questions.question: In science class in Prince George, Nolan's group records a rock sample as 0.070 kg. Nolan says that is the same as 0.7 kg because a zero does not change a decimal. Which statement is correct?
options: Nolan is right: both numbers are read as seven tenths of a kilogram.
Nolan is wrong: 0.070 kg is seventy thousandths, while 0.7 kg is seven tenths, which is ten times larger.
Nolan is wrong: 0.070 kg is really seven thousandths, so it should be written 0.007 kg.
Nolan is right, because the zero between the decimal point and the 7 can be dropped.
questions.explain: Name the place of the last digit: in 0.070 the 7 sits in the hundredths column and the number is seventy thousandths, while 0.7 is seven hundred thousandths — ten times bigger. A zero after the point is a placeholder that holds digits in their columns; only a zero on the far right end can be removed without changing the value.

questions.question: A news graphic shows two BC grants: $7 450 000 000 for housing and $7 450 000 for a neighbourhood park. In the housing grant the digit 4 stands for four hundred million dollars. What does the digit 4 stand for in the park grant, and how do the two values compare?
options: Four hundred thousand dollars, and the housing 4 is worth 100 times as much.
Four million dollars, and the housing 4 is worth 100 times as much.
Four hundred thousand dollars, and the housing 4 is worth 1000 times as much.
Four hundred thousand dollars, and the housing 4 is worth 1 000 000 times as much.
questions.explain: The park grant has seven digits, so its places are millions, hundred thousands, ten thousands — the 4 is worth $400 000, and $400 000 000 is 1000 times that. The trap is assuming millions and billions are only one step apart; each named group is three places, so it is a jump of 1000, not 10 or 100.

questions.question: For a place-value puzzle, Sofia must build one number with 8 in the billions place, 4 in the ten millions place, 3 in the thousandths place, and 0 in every other place. Which number did she build?
questions.explain: Set the billions digit first, then leave a 0 in the empty hundred millions place before the 4, and fill the tenths and hundredths with zeros so the 3 lands in the thousandths column: 8 040 000 000.003. The trap is letting the 4 slide up into hundred millions, or the 3 slide up into hundredths, because a placeholder zero was left out.
